context: Have the orchestrator delegate to a single shared builder rather than assembling its own kwargs, keeping its genuinely CLI-specific concerns (verbosity, resolved output_dir, benchmark-option bridging) as explicit inputs to that builder. Preserve the existing test seam that lets tests patch class resolution. Consider whether constructor_accepts_argument should stop treating a bare **kwargs as universal acceptance, since that is what makes a misrouted kwarg silent.
description: Discovered 2026-08-18 while fixing tpcds-can-never-be-published-official-flag-not-wired, where this duplication directly caused a wrong fix. Benchmark instances are built in two independent places: benchbox/core/benchmark_loader.py get_benchmark_instance() (used by benchbox/core/runner/runner.py:1266) and benchbox/cli/orchestrator.py _get_benchmark_instance() at line 102, which assembles its own kwargs and calls instantiate_benchmark_class() directly at line 159. The CLI uses the second. Each path builds its own optional_kwargs, so any constructor argument must be remembered twice. During the TPC-DS fix, threading the official flag through benchmark_loader alone left every CLI run still emitting compliance_class=unofficial_nonstandard while the unit tests passed - the defect was only caught by running the real CLI and inspecting the bundle. A compliance_mode_kwargs() helper now bridges the two for that one flag, and a test asserts both modules reference it, but the structural duplication remains and the next added kwarg will diverge the same way. Note also that instantiate_benchmark_class() treats a bare **kwargs as accepting any argument (constructor_accepts_argument checks VAR_KEYWORD), so a kwarg sent to the wrong benchmark is silently swallowed rather than raising.

work_units.summary: Design a single builder that covers both call sites without losing the CLI-specific inputs
Migrate the orchestrator to it and delete the duplicated kwarg assembly
Add a test asserting a newly added constructor kwarg reaches instances built via both entry points
